actions.name: Split a bill in Bitcoin: agree who owes what, each pays their own share from their own key
actions.summary: The same agreement as every split — each debtor agrees to their own share with their room key, the creditor that the address is theirs — settled in BTC: each debtor pays their share in satoshis from their own key (wpkh of their muster key), spending their own coins read from their own node, and the creditor's own node confirms each payment when an output pays payTo exactly the share, at the network's confirmation depth. No shared account: nothing on the chain counts or enforces the agreement.

fields.name: chain
fields.means: the CAIP-2 Bitcoin chain every share is paid on, bip122:<genesis prefix> — the policy's qualifier (btc-split@<chain>)

fields.name: asset
fields.means: BTC — a Bitcoin split is paid in bitcoin, never a token

fields.name: total
fields.means: the bill, canonical decimal in satoshis; the creditor's own share is total minus the shares

fields.name: creditor
fields.means: who fronted the bill and is owed: their room identity (64-byte encryption identity, hex)

fields.name: payTo
fields.means: the creditor's receiving address: a segwit address of the chain's network, lowercase — their own wpkh address when they propose (a Bitcoin split is proposed only by whoever fronted it), reviewed and signed

fields.name: shares
fields.means: [{who, amount}] sorted by who, each debtor once, never the creditor, every amount at least Bitcoin's 546-sat dust limit, the sum at most the total

fields.name: quote
fields.means: optional — a bill in another currency (exo-3a4): {currency, fiatTotal in its minor units, fiatDecimals, rateFiat, rateAsset, source, at}; the rate is the proposer's quote, recorded in the log as an external read before anyone agrees ("sources": {"quote": "read"}, invariant 10), and the total must be exactly its conversion

steps.does: Composes the split — even shares round down and the creditor absorbs the remainder (evenShares), or explicit amounts — in satoshis, with their own wpkh address on the chain their own node serves as payTo, under the policy btc-split@<bip122 chain>. The driver refuses anything not in the split's one spelling (non-canonical decimals, unsorted or repeated debtors, the creditor as a debtor, shares above the total or below dust, an asset other than BTC, a payTo of another network, a chain other than the policy's), and on this client's propose path a party who is not a room member. Proposing on someone's behalf is refused: the room's shared addresses are Ethereum ones.

steps.who: each debtor the split names, and the creditor
steps.does: Reviews their own share and agrees in-app: the keystore signs the re-derived materialization with the member's Ed25519 room key. The threshold is every party the effect names — each debtor and the creditor (describeFor) — decoded from the materialization itself, never the room roster, so members the split does not name can never agree, and a later joiner never moves it. A debtor may Deny instead ('that is not my share').
steps.signs: an Ed25519 signature by the debtor's room identity over dCBOR ['muster.split.v1', 'muster.effect.split.v1', chain, asset, total, creditor, payTo, [[who, amount]…], memo]; plus a muster attestation by the same key over P = (context, the materialization, the provenance record)

steps.does: Each debtor pays their own share from their own key: the payment (share, payTo, BTC, chain) is derived by the driver from the agreed effect, never typed. Their client reads their own coins at wpkh(<their muster key>) from their own node (scantxoutset), chooses coins and change (buildSpendFrom), signs every input DER / SIGHASH_ALL over BIP-143 through the keystore, and the node broadcasts; once it is in a block, the debtor's author-signed 'settled' report carries the txid. The creditor's client reads each reported transaction from the creditor's own node and confirms it only when an output pays payTo exactly the share, at the network's confirmation depth (1 on regtest, 6 elsewhere); it never confirms a reference it already confirmed for another share. The fee rate is the member's own, else the node's estimate, else its relay minimum.
steps.signs: each debtor's own Bitcoin spend (their key, through the keystore, BIP-143); each report is signed by its author's room key, bound to the room (authorship)

steps.does: Every share confirmed by the creditor: the fold moves the split to final. A bare submit or final event, which names no author, never moves it — a split's finality is its parts'.

refusals.what: an agreement by anyone the split does not name as a party (another member)
refusals.why: the driver identifies no party for it; it never counts

refusals.what: a split whose shares add up to more than the total, repeat or are unsorted, name the creditor, or are not canonical decimals
refusals.why: invariants 1 and 5: one spelling; refused with its reason, and it canonicalizes to a sentinel no agreement can name

refusals.what: a report that a part was settled, by anyone but that debtor; a confirmation by anyone but the creditor
refusals.why: invariant 9: what the room says about a member is only what that member disclosed

refusals.what: moving a split to final with a bare submit or final event
refusals.why: a split settles in parts; a bare event names no author

refusals.what: submitting a split as one transaction
refusals.why: coordinate_submit answers 'settles-in-parts': each debtor pays their own

refusals.what: paying before every debtor and the creditor agreed, paying twice, or paying a share that is not yours
confirming a reported transaction that pays someone else, or one satoshi more or less than the share, or that is not yet at the network's confirmation depth
refusals.why: the creditor's own read must show it paying payTo exactly the share
the creditor's client refuses a reference it already confirmed for another share

refusals.what: a split in anything but BTC, on a chain other than a known Bitcoin network, paying an address of another network, or with a share below the 546-sat dust limit
refusals.why: the driver refuses it with its reason; it canonicalizes to a sentinel no agreement can name (invariants 1, 5)

refusals.what: paying through a node that serves another chain, or with no node configured
refusals.why: 'your node serves …' / 'no-btc-node': nothing is sent (invariant 8 — the member's own node, never a service's)

refusals.what: a bill in fiat whose total is not exactly its quote's conversion, or whose quote was never recorded as a read
refusals.why: the driver refuses the total with the conversion it expected; without the recorded read the quote is an unaccountable input, so no agreement to it counts ('unaccountable-input', invariant 10)

actions.ui: Room → + → Split with "Settles on" Split (Bitcoin): the total in BTC (8 decimals), who's in, "I'm in it too" → Propose; the split card: each person's share in BTC and where it stands → Agree to my share → Pay my share (from your own coins at your wpkh address, through your own node; no amount or address to type); the creditor's card confirms payments from their own node, or Mark received

claims.claim: You pay exactly the share you agreed, to the address in the split: the payment is derived from the agreed effect, never typed
Only the people a split names can agree to it, and only each can agree to their own share
Nothing makes anyone pay: the room shows who has
Every payment is public on the chain — payer, payee, amount — and several payments to one address close together link the group
Who was at dinner stays in the room: muster never tags a payment on-chain with the split

unverified: the Split composer and card in BTC looked at on a display

actions.name: Settle up in Bitcoin: net several splits into fewer payments
actions.summary: evm.split/settle-up on Bitcoin: the room's agreed, unpaid BTC split shares on one network, netted in satoshis into fewer payments — every member's balance across them kept exactly, each recipient paid only at a wpkh address a split owing them agreed. Every party the covered shares name agrees; each net payment is then a part, paid from the payer's own key through their own node and confirmed by the recipient's own node, exactly as a Bitcoin split's share is. The netting and the cover checks are the chain-agnostic ones the Ethereum settle-up runs; what is Bitcoin's is the asset (BTC only) and the payment.

fields.name: chain
fields.means: the bip122 chain every covered share and every net payment is on — the policy's qualifier

fields.name: asset
fields.means: BTC — a Bitcoin settle-up is in BTC; amounts are satoshis

fields.name: covers
fields.means: [{intent, debtor, creditor, amount, payTo}] sorted by intent then debtor — each an agreed, unpaid share exactly as its split says it

fields.name: transfers
fields.means: [{from, to, payTo, amount}] sorted by from then to — the net payments; conserve every member's balance; each payTo a wpkh address a split owing its recipient agreed

steps.who: any member (a party's proposal is their agreement)
steps.does: In a room whose split policy is btc-split@<bip122 chain>: Settle up the room's open splits. The module gathers every agreed, unpaid, uncovered BTC share on that chain (openParts), nets them (netTransfers) and proposes the settle-up under the same policy. Fewer than two open shares: nothing to net.

steps.who: every party the covered shares name (each debtor and each creditor)
steps.does: Each client checks every cover against its split in the room's log (coordination/covers) before agreeing; then the member's room key signs the settle-up's materialization.
steps.signs: an Ed25519 signature by the party's room identity over dCBOR ['muster.settle-up.v1', 'muster.effect.settle-up.v1', chain, asset, covers, transfers, memo]; plus the muster attestation over P

steps.who: each payer, then each recipient; then each covered share's creditor
steps.does: Each net payment is paid as a Bitcoin split's share is: from the payer's own coins at wpkh(<their muster key>), read from their own node, every input signed DER over BIP-143 through the keystore; the recipient's own node confirms an output paying payTo exactly the amount, at the network's depth. Once final, each creditor's client marks the shares it covered received.
steps.signs: each payer's own Bitcoin transaction; each report signed by its author's room key

steps.does: Every net payment confirmed: the settle-up is final, and the covered shares are marked received; the splits it covered go final.

refusals.what: a Bitcoin settle-up in anything but BTC
refusals.why: the driver refuses it: 'a Bitcoin settle-up is in BTC'

refusals.what: a settle-up whose transfers do not conserve every member's balance, or pay an address no split owing the recipient agreed
refusals.why: the driver's settle-up rules are the same on every chain

actions.ui: Room → + → Split with "Settles on" Split (Bitcoin) → "Settle up the room's open splits instead"; the settle-up card → Agree to settle up → Pay <amount> to <recipient> (from your own coins, through your own node); the recipient's client confirms

claims.claim: Settling up keeps every member's balance exactly and pays each recipient only where their own split said
Nothing makes anyone pay a net payment; the room shows who has
Every net payment is public on the chain — payer, payee, amount

unverified: No test on main yet settles up in BTC end to end: the netting and cover checks are held on Ethereum splits, and a Bitcoin share's payment by split_btc_test — a regtest run of the two together is in progress (settle_up_btc_regtest_e2e)

Netting can leave a payment below the 546-sat dust floor every Bitcoin share must clear (each covered share is at least 546 sat; their difference need not be), and propose does not refuse it; a node will not relay an output below its own dust threshold (294 sat for wpkh at Bitcoin Core's defaults), so such a payment could not land
